title: US 75 Driving Views

pageHeader.title: Driving Views
pageHeader.subTitle: Northbound from I-635 to SH 121, through Richardson, Plano and Allen

text:
The freeway in this area was upgraded and expanded in the 1990s and 2000s. The modernized freeway originally included interior shoulders. The shoulders were converted into pylon-separated HOV lanes around late 2007 or 2008.

In 2023 plans were announced to convert the HOV lanes into so-called "technology lanes". These are toll-free traffic lanes which are restricted to high occupancy vehicles for two hours during weekday peak periods, and are unrestricted general-purpose traffic lanes at all other times. The conversion to technology lanes was completed in summer 2026. As these photos show, the interior lane is designated by parallel stripes.

When these photos were taken on August 8, 2026, the structures of the decorative arches at the DART Silver Line bridge had just been completed (on July 31).

images.caption: At Midpark Lane, just north of Interstate 635
On the overpass at Belt Line
Approaching Renner Road. The new decorative arches are visible ahead.

Construction of the structures of the decorative arches was completed on July 31, 2026, according to a press release from the City of Richardson. The final work to be completed is accent lighting in August and September. The cost of the arches was reported to be around $44 million, with $16 million covered by DART and $28 million covered by the City of Richardson.
The peak arch height is 80 feet above the freeway.
Just north of the Bush Turnpike, with Plano Parkway just ahead (behind the railroad bridge).
At Parker Road. This interchange is a SPUI (single point urban interchange) above the freeway, completed around 2010.
Just south of Exchange Parkway there is an unusual transparent noise barrier. These are common in Europe, but rare in Texas.
